tailMarker.anomalyNote: Resolved by the letter of §3.1 but structurally contested. Rank 8 > 3, and a conditioning ingredient does precede the marker (Myristyl Alcohol @3, a long-chain fatty alcohol named in R1's list), so neither §3.1 anomaly condition is met. However, no cationic surfactant of any kind precedes the marker, and this is a low-water solvent architecture (Propylene Glycol @1, Alcohol denat. @2, Aqua only @5) in which a fragrance level above 1% is entirely plausible. A reviewer who read 'conditioning ingredient' as 'cationic conditioning agent' would set tail_marker: unresolved. See AP-02-BONDTAIL for both readings and their consequences.  ||  PLAUSIBILITY ASSESSMENT (R2, §3.1.1, added under v0.2): IMPLAUSIBLE - tail_marker is UNRESOLVED. Both limbs of the test fire. Limb 1 (architecture comparison): the marker PARFUM @8 outranks every cationic species in the formula - CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @9 is the only cationic surfactant and sits below the marker, as do CETYL ALCOHOL @15 and LAURYL ALCOHOL @14 - so the marker sits before the architecture it is supposed to bound. Limb 2 (low-water / non-emulsion architecture): PROPYLENE GLYCOL @1, ALCOHOL DENAT. @2 and AQUA only @5 is a solvent-continuous, low-water system in which the ~1 % band the marker proxies does not sit where an O/W emulsion's does. Consequences, binding in both directions (§3.1.1 clauses 1-5): the marker may neither disqualify nor qualify; confidence on every affected field is capped at moderate; every affected call routes to human review under `tail_marker_unresolved`; and `unresolved` never auto-decides toward a value. v0.1's AP-02-BONDTAIL recorded exactly this reading as the contested alternative; R2 makes it the rule.  ||  HUMAN RESOLUTION UNDER v0.4 (E11, 2026-09-30): the marker stays `unresolved` and the §3.1.1 rule is unchanged. Nick read the architecture under §14 `tail_marker_unresolved` — the remedy that trigger exists for — and ruled READING B of AP-02-BONDREADINGS for THIS RECORD ONLY: the gluconamide pair @11/@12 is credited as the product's named bonding technology. This is a product-level human resolution, not a change to the general R2 rule that unresolved markers route to human review. Fields the ruling does not name (conditioning_level, weight_potential, care_direction) keep their conservative unresolved-marker reads.

Both paths agree, so the value is robust to the marker question. E2 ceiling: comparative structural intensity potential.
evidenceSignals: MYRISTYL ALCOHOL (rank 3) — long-chain fatty alcohol named in R1's list, at rank 3 of the full list: S2 satisfied on the ordinal read and independent of the marker
DICAPRYLYL CARBONATE (4) + CAPRYLIC/CAPRIC TRIGLYCERIDE (7) — two distinct non-fatty-alcohol lipids, both light-band: S3 satisfied on the ordinal read

CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE (rank 9) — the formula's only cationic surfactant. Under §3.1.1 clause 1 it is read on its own merits rather than disqualified by an unreliable marker; one distinct species either way, so S1 fails under every reading

PARFUM (rank 8) — marker UNRESOLVED: it outranks every cationic and fatty-alcohol species in the formula, on a low-water solvent-continuous architecture (PROPYLENE GLYCOL @1, ALCOHOL DENAT. @2, AQUA @5)
conditioningLevel.derivation: §9.1 under an unresolved marker. S1 = NOT satisfied under either reading (one cationic species exists in the entire formula). S2 = satisfied. S3 = satisfied. R3: S2 + S3 without S1 is `moderate`. Independently, the material-counter-signal conjunct (a) fires — `tail_marker` is `unresolved` — which caps the field at `moderate` regardless.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `moderate`: two convergent routes to the same value (the S1-mandatory rule, and the material-counter-signal cap).
`high` does not apply: S1 fails, and the marker is unresolved — either condition alone forecloses it under R3.
`low` does not apply: S2 and S3 both hold on the ordinal read.
§3.1.1 clause 5 observed: `unresolved` decided nothing here in either direction; it capped confidence and routed the record to review.
counterSignals: `tail_marker: unresolved` (§3.1.1) — MATERIAL counter-signal (a): the above-tail segment the signals were counted on is not reliable. Field listed in `uncertain_fields` and routed under `tail_marker_unresolved`.
Both S3 lipids are light-band esters/triglycerides; this is thin lipid breadth by mask standards, recorded even though S3 is a breadth test rather than a weight test.
Claims '100% stärkeres Haar' and '7x weniger Haarbruch' have no architecture behind them in the credited segment — recorded in `hinweise`, moving nothing (§11 step 4).
limitations: A three-step concentration scale is at the edge of INCI support; no published dataset maps INCI patterns to validated low/medium/high thresholds (§9.1 honest limitation).
Rank is used qualitatively only. EU Art. 19 hides the 1 % boundary; no percentage, ratio, dose or deposited amount is inferable.
A 7-second stated dwell sits outside every tested contact time; `dwell_efficacy: unknown`, never extrapolated in either direction (evidence §3, `express_dwell_unknown`).

An absence-based `low` on an unreadable segment would hand this product a lean fit prior, and therefore a fine-hair recommendation, on evidence we have just declared unreliable (§1.1, §9.2). E2 ceiling: weight deposition potential, never measured finish.

MYRISTYL ALCOHOL (3), LAURYL ALCOHOL (14), CETYL ALCOHOL (15) — three long-chain fatty-alcohol species in the list; on the ordinal read the fatty base is not thin, so even a readable segment would not clearly deliver the leanness test

`low` does not apply — and this is the substantive change from v0.1, which recorded `low`. adjudicationPoints.title: CLOSED by E11 (2026-09-30) — READING B APPLIED per Nick: the gluconamide pair is credited on this record; both readings stay documented
adjudicationPoints.body: Both readings are retained as documentation. READING A (conservative; APPLIED under v0.2 and v0.3, now SUPERSEDED): the gluconamide pair HYDROXYPROPYLGLUCONAMIDE @11 + HYDROXYPROPYLAMMONIUM GLUCONATE @12 sits ordinally below PARFUM @8 and is not credited — bond_route `none`, repair_support_level `low`, primary_focus `general`, care_direction `moisture`. READING B (architecture-first; APPLIED per Nick 2026-09-30, E11): in a low-water solvent system the ~1 % band does not sit where the Parfum does; the pair is the product's named bonding technology, declared as a pair exactly as the Ashland FiberHance system is supplied, and it sits above the keratin and the two secondary fatty alcohols. Nick ruled E11 reading the architecture per §14 `tail_marker_unresolved` — the human resolution that trigger routes to. It is a product-level ruling and does NOT change the general R2 rule that unresolved markers route to human review; the marker stays `unresolved`. Effects applied, each re-verified on this record's own INCI: bond_route none → `gluconamide`; repair_support_level low → `high`; bond_specific_support claim_only → chemistry_candidate; focus cascade re-run → primary_focus `repair` (focus_care_verdict repair_supported); all at `moderate` confidence with the `tail_marker` hinweise note retained. care_direction stays `moisture` (§6 rule 4: the bond token is not a protein-film route; HYDROLYZED KERATIN @13 alone is not a material R5 route). ONE listed effect was NOT applied: damage_fit stays {healthy, moderately_damaged}, because §9.7 grants the specialist row only under conditioning_level `high` and this record's conditioning_level is `moderate` under every reading — see AP-02-DAMAGEFITECHO. The former asymmetry with #04 (identical pair at 8/9 above a plausible marker, credited without argument) is resolved: both siblings now credit the pair.

adjudicationPoints.title: The cohort's only `lightness` selection is withdrawn, on the readability rule rather than on the architecture
adjudicationPoints.body: v0.1 selected `lightness` as this product's primary focus — the one selection of that value anywhere in the cohort, and the answer §18 open question 4 was watching for. Under v0.2 it is withdrawn, because `lightness` requires `weight_potential: low` and R4 makes `low` a positive leanness test that §9.2 declares unavailable on an unreadable above-tail segment. The product is still, on any substantive reading, the lightest thing in the cohort: a solvent-continuous express serum with no butter, no heavy triglyceride, no occlusive and no silicone. So the answer to 'is lightness ever selected in this category' is now: not on this cohort, and not because the architecture failed the test but because the marker did. That is the conservative-failure invariant working as designed (§1.1: an absence-based `low` would hand a fine-hair prior to a formula we cannot read), but it means the field's reachability is entirely untested by this run and must be carried into the freeze gate.
adjudicationPoints.source: §9.2 (R4) readability precondition; §9.5.2 step 3 `lightness`; §18 open questions 2 and 4
